title: Agnipath Scheme 2026 - Agniveer Salary ₹30-40K, Seva Nidhi ₹11.71 Lakh, How to Apply
meta_description: Agnipath scheme 2026 complete guide - Agniveer salary ₹30,000-40,000/month, ₹11.71 lakh Seva Nidhi after 4 years, 25% retention for permanent commission, eligibility 17.5-21 years, online application at joinindianarmy.nic.in.

hero.one_liner: 4-year military service in Indian Armed Forces with ₹30,000-40,000 monthly salary and ₹11.71 lakh tax-free Seva Nidhi on completion

what_is_it: The Agnipath Scheme is a military recruitment program launched on 14 June 2022 for the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force. Under this scheme, young Indians (called 'Agniveers') are recruited for a 4-year service period. After 4 years, 25% of Agniveers are selected for permanent enrollment (15-year minimum service), while the remaining 75% are released with a tax-free Seva Nidhi (service fund) of approximately ₹11.71 lakh.

Agniveers receive an attractive salary package: ₹30,000/month in the first year, increasing to ₹40,000/month in the fourth year. Of this, 30% is automatically contributed to the Seva Nidhi corpus, with the government matching it equally. The Seva Nidhi (approximately ₹5 lakh from the Agniveer + ₹5 lakh from government + interest = ₹11.71 lakh) is paid as a lump sum upon completion of 4 years.

The scheme was introduced to reduce the average age of armed forces personnel (previously 32 years) to about 26 years, making the military younger, fitter, and more technologically adaptable. It also provides military training, discipline, and marketable skills to millions of youth - even those who don't continue in the forces benefit from the experience, skill certifications, and financial corpus.

As of March 2026, recruitment continues through periodic notifications. The scheme combines patriotic service with financial security and skill development. For released Agniveers, there are additional benefits: priority in CAPF (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP) recruitment, age relaxation in government exams, preference in state police jobs, and skill certifications recognized across industries.

eligibility.value: 17.5 to 23 years (originally 17.5-21, extended to 23 for early batches)

eligibility.label: Education (Army)
eligibility.value: 10th pass for General Duty, 12th pass (Science) for Technical, 12th for Clerk/SKT

eligibility.label: Education (Navy)
eligibility.value: 12th pass with Maths & Physics for Senior Secondary Recruit (SSR), 10th pass for Matric Recruit (MR)

eligibility.label: Education (Air Force)
eligibility.value: 12th pass with Maths & Physics, minimum 50% aggregate and 50% in English

eligibility.label: Physical standards
eligibility.value: Height: 170 cm (men), 152 cm (women). Weight proportionate to height. Vision: 6/6 without glasses (varies by trade). No tattoos on inner arms.

eligibility.label: Citizenship
eligibility.value: Indian citizen. Must not be married at time of enrollment (can marry during 4-year service with permission)

eligibility.label: Medical
eligibility.value: Must pass military medical examination - no chronic diseases, bone deformities, or disqualifying conditions. TB, cardiac issues, diabetes: disqualifying.

extra_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
extra_sections.content: Men and women aged 17.5 to 21 years (Navy) / 17.5 to 23 years (Army, Airforce) who passed 10th/12th depending on trade. No experience required. Height/weight and medical tests are strict - check official notification.

extra_sections.caption: Every Agniveer follows one of three paths after 4 years
extra_sections.description: The retention ratio is decided purely on merit - performance during training, annual ratings, fitness tests. Retained Agniveers become regular soldiers with full pension benefits after 15 more years.

extra_sections.heading: Salary Breakdown & Seva Nidhi Accumulation Over 4 Years
What Happens After 4 Years - Three Scenarios
content:
Scenario 1: Selected for Permanent Service (25% of Agniveers)

After 4 years, approximately 25% of Agniveers are selected for permanent enrollment in the regular armed forces based on merit, performance during service, physical fitness, and organizational requirements.

These Agniveers continue for a minimum total service of 15 years (so 11 more years after Agnipath) with full military pay (₹40,000-60,000/month, increasing with rank), allowances, pension after 20 years, and all service benefits.
Permanent selection depends on: Performance appraisal (65%), medical fitness, organizational vacancies, and officer potential assessment.

Scenario 2: Released with Seva Nidhi (75% of Agniveers)

The remaining 75% of Agniveers complete their 4-year service and receive the Seva Nidhi package. Total Seva Nidhi = Agniveer's contribution (₹5.02 lakh over 4 years) + Government's matching contribution (₹5.02 lakh) + Accrued interest on the fund ≈ ₹11.71 lakh (tax-free).
This amount is credited to their bank account as a lump sum upon discharge.

Using the Seva Nidhi Corpus

Released Agniveers can use ₹11.71 lakh for: (1) Starting their own business (with preference under PM Mudra, Stand Up India), (2) Pursuing higher education (polytechnic, bachelor's degree, professional courses), (3) Meeting family needs or personal investment, (4) Down payment on a house (combined with bank loan), (5) Skill certification courses in civil sector jobs.
No restrictions on usage - the money is completely theirs.

extra_sections.heading: Benefits After Agnipath Completion
content:
Priority in Government Jobs

Agniveers get 10% reservation in recruitment for CAPF (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB) across India. Additionally, many states have announced 10% reservations in state police recruitment for ex-Agniveers.
Age relaxation: 3 years additional age relaxation (beyond normal limit) in central government exams (SSC, Railways, UPSC, etc.).

Skill Certifications & Market Credibility

Agniveers receive official skill certificates for their trade learned during service (e.g., vehicle maintenance, communications, logistics, ammunition handling, etc.). These NSQF-aligned certifications are recognized by employers and enhance employability in private sector.
Certificate also certifies physical fitness, discipline, and reliability - valued across industries.

Veteran Identity & Community

Agniveers become recognized veterans with service medals, discharge certificate, and veteran benefits. They join a nationwide network of ex-service personnel with mutual support and networking opportunities.
Many employers actively recruit ex-military personnel for their discipline and training background.

Bank Loans at Preferential Rates

Agniveers can access bank loans (Mudra, housing, auto, personal) at preferential rates. Banks treat military service experience as favorable for creditworthiness.
Many Agniveers use their Seva Nidhi + bank loan to start businesses (e.g., franchise, restaurant, transport, retail).

Private Sector Opportunities

Major employers actively recruit ex-Agniveers: IT companies (prefer technical skills), logistics/transportation (experienced personnel), private security firms, hospitality (discipline and customer service), manufacturing, and civil aviation (technical roles). Some companies have committed to hiring at least 5-10% ex-Agniveers.

steps.title: Online registration
steps.description: Register at joinindianarmy.nic.in (Army), joinindiannavy.gov.in (Navy), or official Air Force portal. Fill personal details, educational qualifications, physical measurements, and choose your preferred trade.

steps.title: Physical Fitness Test (PFT) at rally point
steps.description: PFT is conducted at designated rally locations in your district. Tests include: 1.6 km run (must complete within 5 min 30 sec for Army), pull-ups, balance test, standing broad jump, and other physical standards. PFT is elimination round - only 30-40% of candidates pass this stage.

steps.title: Medical examination
steps.description: Thorough medical checkup including vision test, hearing test, dental examination, cardiovascular assessment, chest X-ray, and musculoskeletal evaluation. Any chronic condition (diabetes, hypertension requiring medication), bone deformity, or disqualifying condition leads to rejection.

steps.title: Common Entrance Examination (CEE)
steps.description: Written examination covering general knowledge, mathematics, reasoning, and English (60-90 minutes). Pattern varies by service (Army, Navy, Air Force) and trade. Merit list is prepared based on PFT + CEE score. Candidates in top merit list are called for document verification.

steps.title: Document verification and enrollment
steps.description: Selected candidates (typically top 5,000-10,000 from 500,000+ applicants) submit original documents (birth certificate, school certificates, Aadhaar, caste certificate if applicable) for verification. After successful verification, enrollment is confirmed. Training begins at respective training establishments (Army: various regimental training centers, Navy: INS Chilka, Air Force: Air Force Academy/stations).

extra_sections.heading: The Real Challenge
extra_sections.content: Only 25% are retained for regular service after 4 years. The other 75% return to civilian life with ₹11.71 lakh Seva Nidhi. Have a clear plan for what you'll do if not retained - college, business, or CAPF/police exams.

extra_sections.heading: What Is the Agnipath Scheme - Complete Breakdown
content: The Agnipath scheme is India's new military recruitment model launched in June 2022 by the Ministry of Defence. It replaces the traditional recruitment system for soldiers, sailors, and airmen in the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force with a four-year contractual service model under which recruits are called Agniveers.

Under this scheme, young Indians aged 17.5 to 21 years are recruited for a four-year period of service. After completing four years, up to 25% of each batch will be selected for permanent enrollment in the armed forces for a full 15-year tenure. The remaining 75% will be released from service with a one-time Seva Nidhi (service fund) package and the skills, training, and experience gained during their military service.

The scheme was introduced to address the rising age profile of the Indian armed forces, reduce the massive pension bill that consumes over 25% of the defence budget, and create a younger, fitter military force. By recruiting soldiers for short tenures and retaining only the best performers, the scheme aims to bring in fresh talent continuously while keeping the average age of the force significantly lower than the previous system.

extra_sections.heading: Seva Nidhi Package and Financial Benefits
content: Agniveers receive a customized monthly salary package starting at Rs 30,000 per month in the first year, increasing to Rs 33,000 in the second year, Rs 36,500 in the third year, and Rs 40,000 in the fourth year. A portion of this salary (30%) is contributed by the Agniveer to the Seva Nidhi fund, and the government matches this contribution with an equal amount.

After completing four years of service, the accumulated Seva Nidhi fund amounts to approximately Rs 11.71 lakh including the government's matching contribution and interest earned. This lump sum payment is tax-free and is designed to provide a financial foundation for Agniveers transitioning back to civilian life.

During service, Agniveers receive a non-contributory life insurance cover of Rs 48 lakh. In case of death during service, the next of kin receives the full insurance amount plus the accumulated Seva Nidhi with interest. For disability during service, compensation is provided based on the percentage of disability as per government norms.

The Seva Nidhi amount of Rs 11.71 lakh, combined with the skills certification, physical fitness, discipline, and leadership training gained during four years of military service, is positioned as a strong foundation for starting a business, pursuing higher education, or securing employment in the private or public sector.

extra_sections.heading: Recruitment Process and Selection Criteria
content: Agniveer recruitment follows a multi-stage selection process conducted by the respective service recruitment organizations - Army Recruiting Offices for the Indian Army, Indian Navy Recruitment portals, and the Indian Air Force's CASB for air force positions.

For the Indian Army, candidates register online at joinindianarmy.nic.in and appear for a rally-based recruitment process. The stages include physical fitness tests (1.6 km run in specified time, pull-ups, long jump, balance test), physical measurement verification (height, weight, chest), medical examination, and a Common Entrance Exam (CEE) testing General Knowledge, Mathematics, General Science, and Reasoning.

The Indian Navy and Air Force conduct their own online examinations followed by physical fitness tests and medical examinations. The Navy recruits Agniveers for specific trades including seaman, mechanic, and artificer categories. The Air Force recruits for technical and non-technical trades.

Educational qualifications vary by service and trade. Army Agniveers in the General Duty category require Class 10 pass. Technical and clerical categories require Class 12 pass with specific subjects. Navy and Air Force positions typically require Class 12 with Science subjects for technical trades. All candidates must meet physical fitness standards specific to their service branch.

extra_sections.heading: Life as an Agniveer - Training and Service
content: Selected Agniveers undergo rigorous military training at the respective service training establishments. Army Agniveers train at regimental centers for approximately 10 to 31 weeks depending on the arm and trade. Navy Agniveers train at INS Chilka and other naval training establishments. Air Force Agniveers train at the Air Force Training Command facilities.

Training covers weapon handling, physical fitness, military discipline, field craft, basic combat skills, and trade-specific technical training. The training is designed to produce soldiers capable of active combat deployment within a compressed timeline compared to the traditional longer training periods.

During the four-year service period, Agniveers serve in active military units and can be deployed in any operational area including forward positions, counter-insurgency zones, and peacekeeping missions. They perform the same duties as regular soldiers, sailors, and airmen during their tenure. The experience gained during active service - leadership, teamwork, discipline, technical skills, and crisis management - is invaluable regardless of whether they are retained permanently.

Agniveers who demonstrate exceptional performance during their four-year tenure are eligible for permanent enrollment. The selection for the 25% permanent slots is based on merit - combining performance evaluations, physical fitness scores, discipline record, and aptitude assessments. Those selected transition to the regular service cadre and serve the remaining tenure of their engagement with standard career progression.
For more details, see our guide on NDA Exam 2026.
For more details, see our guide on PM KUSUM Yojana.

extra_sections.heading: Post-Service Opportunities for Agniveers
extra_sections.content: Agniveers who complete their four-year service receive certified skills and qualifications recognized by the National Skills Qualification Framework. Several state governments have announced reservation for ex-Agniveers in state police and paramilitary recruitment. The central government has reserved 10% vacancies in CAPFs and Assam Rifles for ex-Agniveers. Multiple corporate groups including Tata, Mahindra, and Reliance have announced preferential hiring for ex-Agniveers. Additionally, ex-Agniveers receive priority in bank loan schemes for entrepreneurship and are eligible for various skill development courses funded by the government.

extra_sections.heading: Controversies and Criticisms of the Agnipath Scheme
content: The Agnipath scheme generated significant controversy when announced, with protests in several states from aspiring military candidates who had been preparing for traditional recruitment. The primary concerns centered around job security, pension benefits, and the future of the 75% Agniveers who would be released after four years.

Critics argue that four years is insufficient to develop fully trained, experienced soldiers and that the constant turnover creates operational challenges for units. Defence analysts have debated whether the scheme reduces combat effectiveness by replacing experienced personnel with younger but less experienced recruits every four years.

Supporters counter that the scheme modernizes military recruitment along the lines practiced by several NATO countries, reduces the unsustainable pension burden, and creates a large pool of disciplined, trained young people who can contribute to the economy. The younger average age of the force is expected to improve operational fitness and adaptability.

The scheme is now into its second cycle of recruitment, and the initial batch of Agniveers is nearing the end of their first year of service. The real impact of the scheme - on military readiness, on the post-service career outcomes of released Agniveers, and on the overall quality of India's armed forces - will become clearer over the next 3 to 5 years as the first batches complete their tenure.

extra_sections.heading: Preparation Strategy for Agniveer Selection
content: Physical fitness preparation is paramount since it is the first elimination stage. Start running daily at least 3 months before the expected recruitment rally date. For the 1.6 km run, aim to consistently finish under 5 minutes in practice - the actual qualifying time is 5 minutes 30 seconds to 6 minutes 30 seconds depending on the category, but exam-day conditions add time. Practice pull-ups, long jump, and balance exercises regularly.

For the Common Entrance Exam, the academic preparation covers Class 10 and 12 level subjects depending on the trade you are applying for. General Duty requires Class 10 Mathematics, General Science, and General Knowledge. Technical and clerical categories require Class 12 level questions in relevant subjects. Use Arihant's or Disha's Agniveer preparation books that are specifically designed for the CEE pattern.

Medical fitness is non-negotiable and cannot be improved with last-minute preparation. Vision must be within prescribed limits, hearing must be normal, and there should be no chronic conditions that affect physical capability. Get a preliminary medical checkup from a military doctor or qualified physician to identify any issues early. Dental problems, flat feet, and vision issues are the most common causes of medical rejection.

extra_sections.heading: Agniveer vs Traditional Military Recruitment - Key Differences
content: The traditional military recruitment system offered a minimum service period of 15 to 20 years with full pension, gratuity, and ex-serviceman benefits upon retirement. Soldiers who completed their full tenure received a monthly pension for life, which provided lifelong financial security. The pension system, however, created a massive fiscal burden - defence pension currently exceeds Rs 1.5 lakh crore annually.

Under Agnipath, only the 25% retained Agniveers receive the full career benefits including pension. The 75% released after four years receive the Seva Nidhi lump sum but no pension, no ex-serviceman status, and no Canteen Stores Department access. This is the most significant trade-off and the primary source of criticism from aspirants and veterans.

The training period has been compressed compared to traditional recruitment. Traditional soldiers received longer training periods - up to one year for some arms - allowing deeper skill development. Agniveers receive shorter but intensive training designed to make them operationally deployable faster. Whether this compressed training produces equally effective soldiers is an ongoing debate within the defence establishment.

From a career flexibility perspective, the Agnipath system has one advantage: it allows young people to experience military life without committing to a 15-year career. For individuals who discover that military life does not suit them, exiting after four years with the Seva Nidhi fund is a structured option that did not exist in the previous system, where leaving before the minimum tenure involved complex discharge procedures.

extra_sections.text: Agnipath is not the end of military careers in India - it is a new beginning that offers four years of world-class military training, discipline, and an Rs 11.71 lakh financial package that most entry-level jobs in India cannot match.

extra_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Agnipath
content: Can women apply for Agnipath? Yes, women are eligible for Agniveer recruitment in all three services. The Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force conduct separate recruitment drives with physical fitness standards specific to women candidates. Women Agniveers serve in the same units and undergo the same training as male Agniveers, with adjusted physical standards where applicable.

What happens after four years if I am not selected for permanent enrollment? You receive the Seva Nidhi package of approximately Rs 11.71 lakh, certified skills qualifications, and exit from service. You are eligible for reservations in CAPF and state police recruitment, priority in corporate hiring programs, and subsidized loans for entrepreneurship. Your four years of military service and the skills certificate serve as strong credentials for civilian employment.

Can I apply for Agniveer recruitment in multiple services? No, each recruitment cycle allows application to only one service - Army, Navy, or Air Force. However, if you are not selected in one service's recruitment, you can apply to a different service in the next recruitment cycle as long as you remain within the eligible age limit.

Is there any reservation in Agniveer recruitment? Yes, standard government reservation policies for SC, ST, and OBC-NCL candidates apply to Agniveer recruitment. The physical and academic selection criteria remain the same across all categories, but the reservation percentages in final selection follow constitutional norms.

What educational qualifications are needed? Requirements vary by service and trade. Indian Army General Duty requires Class 10 pass. Army Technical requires Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. Army Clerk requires Class 12 with 60% aggregate. Navy and Air Force positions typically require Class 12 with Science subjects for technical trades.

extra_sections.heading: State Government Benefits for Ex-Agniveers
content: Multiple state governments have announced additional benefits for Agniveers who complete their four-year service, creating a support ecosystem beyond the central government's provisions.

Several states including Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, and Uttarakhand have announced reservation for ex-Agniveers in state police and paramilitary recruitment. Some states have gone further - offering age relaxation, bonus marks in competitive exams, and priority in state government job applications for ex-Agniveers.

Skill development programs specifically designed for ex-Agniveers are being established by state skill development missions. These programs offer advanced training in sectors like logistics, security management, information technology, and infrastructure construction - leveraging the discipline and work ethic that military service instills.

Entrepreneurship support through subsidized loans and mentorship is available in several states. Financial institutions have created specific loan products for ex-Agniveers, recognizing their discipline and the Seva Nidhi capital as indicators of lower default risk. The combination of Rs 11.71 lakh Seva Nidhi, subsidized loans, and government-sponsored training creates a viable path for ex-Agniveers to become self-employed.

how_to_apply.title: Register online at service-specific portal
how_to_apply.description: Army: joinindianarmy.nic.in, Navy: joinindiannavy.gov.in, Air Force: official portal. Fill personal and educational details.

how_to_apply.title: Watch for rally/recruitment notifications
how_to_apply.description: Notifications are published on official portals and in Employment News magazine. Check every month as recruitment happens in batches (typically 3-4 batches per year). Some states have multiple rallies.

how_to_apply.title: Appear for Physical Fitness Test at rally point
how_to_apply.description: Carry all original documents, 10 passport photos, running shoes, and sports clothing. PFT usually happens on same day as registration or next day.

how_to_apply.title: Clear medical + written exam + verification
how_to_apply.description: If you pass PFT, you're called for medical exam and CEE within 1-2 weeks. Merit-based selection determines final enrollment.

important_alert.text: Agnipath recruitment notifications are published periodically - not continuous. Check official portals at joinindianarmy.nic.in regularly. Beware of fraudsters claiming to arrange selection for money or 'coaching' - all recruitment is through official government portals only. No agent or coaching institute can guarantee selection.

faqs.question: Is Agnipath only for men?
faqs.answer: No. Women are eligible for Agnipath recruitment in all three services (Army, Navy, Air Force). The Indian Air Force and Navy have already recruited women Agniveers since 2022. The Indian Army has opened most categories to women. Physical standards differ between genders (e.g., height: men 170 cm, women 152 cm), but opportunities are equal.

faqs.question: What if I'm not selected for permanent service after 4 years?
faqs.answer: You receive ₹11.71 lakh Seva Nidhi (tax-free), a service discharge certificate, and skill certifications recognized nationwide. You get priority (10% reservation) in CAPF recruitment (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP). Many states have announced 10% reservation in state police recruitment for ex-Agniveers. Private companies actively hire ex-military personnel. The Seva Nidhi helps you start a business or pursue education.

faqs.question: Can I prepare for other competitive exams during 4-year service?
faqs.answer: Yes. Agniveers get study leave and access to education facilities. Many Agniveers prepare for NDA, CDS, CAPF (Officer), SSC, and state PSC exams during service. The military training and discipline actually improve exam performance. Success in exams while still serving is fast-tracked to officer rank or alternate career.

faqs.question: Is there age relaxation for Agniveers in government exams?
faqs.answer: Yes. Government has announced 3-year age relaxation for Agniveers appearing in central government recruitment exams (CAPF, SSC, Railways, UPSC, etc.). Additionally, the Agniveer's 4-year service counts toward age requirements in some job categories. Many states have announced additional age relaxation (5-7 years) in state police and government job exams.

faqs.question: What happens to the Seva Nidhi if an Agniveer dies during service?
faqs.answer: If an Agniveer dies during service, the family receives: (1) ₹48 lakh non-contributory life insurance payout + (2) Full accumulated Seva Nidhi corpus (approximately ₹11.71 lakh at completion, or proportionate amount if death occurs earlier) + (3) Ex-gratia compensation as applicable to armed forces personnel + (4) Family pension in some cases. The family is not left without financial support.

faqs.question: Do released Agniveers get pension?
faqs.answer: No. Released Agniveers who complete 4 years and are NOT selected for permanent service do not receive pension. Only those selected for permanent enrollment and completing 20+ years of total service get military pension (approximately 50% of last salary + DA). The Seva Nidhi (₹11.71 lakh) is the financial benefit for released Agniveers, meant to cover transition and initial civilian career costs.

faqs.question: Can I prepare for Agnipath while working or studying?
faqs.answer: Yes. Agnipath is open to anyone aged 17.5-23. You can prepare while in college or working a part-time job. However, once selected, you must complete 4 years of full-time military service - you cannot work another job simultaneously. Many candidates prepare for Agnipath as their primary career goal while completing 12th standard or early college.

faqs.question: What if I fail PFT? Can I try again?
faqs.answer: If you fail PFT in one rally, you can try in the next recruitment notification (typically 1-2 months later). There is no limit on number of attempts as long as you're within the age window (17.5-23 years). Many candidates succeed on 2nd or 3rd attempt after physical conditioning.

faqs.question: What is the salary of Agniveer in 2026?
faqs.answer: Agniveer salary starts at ₹30,000/month in Year 1 and increases to ₹40,000/month by Year 4. Additionally, 30% of salary is deducted as Seva Nidhi contribution, matched by the government, giving you ₹11.71 lakh tax-free after 4 years.

faqs.question: What happens after 4 years in Agnipath scheme?
faqs.answer: After 4 years, 25% of Agniveers are selected for permanent commission in the armed forces (15-year service). The remaining 75% are released with ₹11.71 lakh Seva Nidhi (tax-free), skills certificate, and preference in other government jobs.

faqs.question: Can Agniveers apply for other government jobs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ex-Agniveers (after 4 years) get age relaxation and preference in CAPFs (CRPF, BSF, CISF), state police, defence PSUs, and other government recruitments. Many departments have reserved 10% vacancies for ex-Agniveers.
